title: Tool-trust walk gaps: shebang interpreter, shared libraries, and the full PATH given to the child
description: Finding 6 of the opum-ai/ward-cli#308 Opus review, outside DEC-262 (a10) as ruled. The walk covers the resolved tpm2_* path to its final regular file and every ancestor. It does not cover (1) the interpreter named by a script tool shebang, (2) the shared libraries a tool loads, or (3) the PATH the child receives: runTool gives the full search path, so a trusted tool that execs a helper by name bypasses the walk. Needs a design decision from opum-doc before code: walk the shebang interpreter, restrict the child PATH to the walked tool directories, or accept and record the residual. Raise as an A/B through the leader; do not decide here.
implementationNotes:
RULING DEC-262 (a12) from opum-doc, relayed by the leader, VERBATIM. It STARTS ONLY AFTER MONDAY 2026-11-09 PLAN APPROVAL; no code before then. Order: this task is its own PR (with an Opus review) BEFORE slice 2b part 2 (seal/unseal); no real key is piped until it lands.

"1. Built environment: the child gets an environment Ward builds; it does not inherit the parent's. PATH = the resolved tool's directory + /usr/bin + /bin, and every directory in it must pass the (a10)/(a11) walk, or Ward refuses tool_untrusted naming that directory. Only Ward-set variables are passed (TPM2TOOLS_*, the TCTI Ward chooses), plus LANG/LC_ALL=C. No LD_*, no DYLD_*, and not the parent's PATH or HOME.
2. Shebang: if the final file starts with "#!", the interpreter must be an absolute path that passes the walk, or Ward refuses tool_untrusted naming it. "#!/usr/bin/env X" is accepted only by walking env; rule 1 confines X to walked directories. A relative interpreter is refused.
3. Shared libraries: a recorded residual, not built. Rule 1 removes LD_PRELOAD and LD_LIBRARY_PATH. An ELF RUNPATH pointing at a directory another user can write is a packaging defect outside AC2; note it in the threat-model ADR, and do not parse ELF.
Tests, both directions. Accept: a symlinked multicall install, run with the built environment. Reject: an interpreter in a writable directory; a relative interpreter; a helper that is findable only on the parent's PATH.
Order: WCLI-164 is its own PR before 2b part 2 (seal/unseal), with an Opus review. No real key is piped until it lands."
